title: Coworker stole my pitch
author: Storytime
hook: My coworker presented my idea to our biggest client as her own. Then the client asked her one question.
story: I work at a small marketing agency. Two weeks ago, I pitched a holiday campaign idea to my coworker Brooke over lunch. A slogan, a whole concept. She said, that's cute. Last Thursday, we had a meeting with our biggest client, a bakery chain. Brooke stood up and presented my idea. Word for word. My slogan. My concept. She didn't even look at me. My boss loved it. I sat there, shaking. Then the client's marketing director, a woman named Tess, smiled and asked Brooke one question. She said, I love the slogan. Rise and shine, sweet thing. Where did that come from? Brooke said, oh, it just came to me. Tess laughed and said, really? Because that's what my college roommate used to sing to wake me up every morning. For four years. Then she looked straight at me and said, hi, Megan. Tess was my college roommate. I hadn't seen her in eight years. I didn't even know she worked there. The room went silent. My boss looked at Brooke. Brooke looked at the floor. After the meeting, my boss asked me to lead the account. Brooke hasn't spoken to me since. Should I have said something sooner?
caption: she stole the wrong slogan 🧁 #storytime
sound: a confident, sassy beat with a satisfying drop at very low volume
why: Coworkers undermining each other is trending in workplace TikTok right now, the slogan is a planted clue, the roommate reveal is satisfying karma, and the question invites people to share their own stories.

title: My cat has a second family
author: Storytime
hook: My cat has been living a double life. My neighbor thinks he's her cat. And now she wants custody.
story: I adopted my cat, Pickles, three years ago. Orange, chubby, lazy. Or so I thought. A few months ago, he started coming home at night smelling like expensive perfume. He stopped finishing his food. He gained weight anyway. Then one day, he came home wearing a tiny knitted bow tie. I did not buy him a bow tie. So I put a little tracker on his collar. Every morning at eight, he walks next door. To Mrs. Fernsby's house. She's seventy-eight. And every evening at six, he walks home. I knocked on her door. She opened it, holding Pickles. She said, oh, have you met Duke? I said, that's my cat. She looked at me like I was crazy. She said, no, dear, this is Duke. He's been coming here for a year. He has his own bed. His own vet. His own Instagram. Duke's Instagram has more followers than mine. She showed me a photo album. Duke at Christmas. Duke at her birthday. Duke in a little Halloween costume. Mrs. Fernsby lives alone. Her husband passed last year. Pickles shows up every single morning to sit with her. Now she's offered to pay half his food bills, if we share him. Should I agree to joint custody?
caption: my cat has a second family. and a bow tie 🐈 #storytime
sound: a playful, sneaky pizzicato melody at very low volume
why: Pet stories reach huge audiences, the bow tie is a funny clue, the double life reveal is hilarious then heartwarming, and joint custody invites lots of joke comments.

title: I swapped places with my twin on her first date
author: Storytime
hook: In college, I went on my twin sister's first date pretending to be her. She married him. He still doesn't know.
story: My twin sister Claire and I are identical. In college, she had a first date with a guy named Owen. She panicked an hour before and begged me to go instead. Just to see if he was nice. So I went. As Claire. We had pizza, we walked by the river, and he told me about his grandpa's farm. It was honestly perfect. The next date, Claire went herself. Owen never noticed. They got married five years later. Their tenth anniversary is next month. Last week, Owen called me. He wants to surprise Claire by recreating their first date. Same pizza place. Same walk. He said, but I can't remember what we ordered, and Claire says she can't either. Can you ask her? I already know. Half pepperoni, half pineapple. Because I ordered it. Claire doesn't know anything about that night. She never asked. Now Owen is planning a toast called, the night I knew she was the one. About a night with me. Do I tell my sister, or let him give the toast?
caption: the night he knew she was the one was me 👯 #storytime
sound: a slow, suspenseful romantic piano at very low volume
why: Twin swap secrets are irresistible, the forgotten pizza order is the perfect clue, the anniversary toast raises the stakes, and the tell or not question sparks big debates.
